title: Slapo: A Schedule Language for Progressive Optimization of Large Deep Learning Model Training
problem: Deep learning frameworks face a critical tradeoff between usability and training performance. Dynamic graph frameworks like PyTorch enable flexible model development but suffer from sub-optimal training performance, while static graph optimizers (XLA) and specialized distributed training systems (DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM) achieve high performance at the cost of reduced flexibility.
motivation: Training efficiency is crucial for large deep learning models, making it essential to address the usability-performance tradeoff.
method: Slapo introduces a domain-specific schedule language that enables progressive optimization of DL model training. Developers express optimization strategies declaratively, and the system progressively applies optimizations to improve training performance. The language-based approach allows fine-grained control over scheduling decisions while maintaining the flexibility of dynamic computation graphs.
key_novelty: A domain-specific schedule language that enables progressive optimization, allowing developers to balance the flexibility of dynamic frameworks with the performance characteristics of static optimizers.
contributions: Schedule language for declaratively expressing progressive optimization strategies for DL model training
System that progressively applies optimizations while preserving code flexibility and usability
Approach bridging the tradeoff between dynamic graph flexibility and static optimization performance
limitations: Limitations not discussed in provided abstract
primary_theme: Deep learning training optimization via declarative scheduling
